request.state: {"result":"An ERC-20 token approval is a permission you grant on-chain allowing a specific app or contract (a \"spender\") to move a set amount of a particular token from your wallet. Apps ask for it because a smart contract can't pull tokens from your wallet without your consent — before a swap, deposit, or trade, you sign an approval so the contract can transfer the tokens you've agreed to use. The risk comes from approving an unlimited amount: the permission stays active until you change it, so if the app's contract is later exploited or the team turns malicious, the spender can drain that token from your wallet at any time, even long after your original transaction. To limit the risk, approve only the amount you need rather than the maximum, and review and revoke old approvals periodically using a tool such as your wallet's built-in approval manager or a service like Revoke.cash, which lets you set an allowance to zero or reset it to a smaller figure (though revoking itself costs gas).","task":{"brief":"Explain token approvals and their risk\n\nExplain what an ERC-20 token approval is, why apps ask for one, the risk of approving an unlimited amount, and how a user can limit or remove an approval.
